thread:
Elly: FYI — AcroHealth reporting a sudden spike of connection resets and 5xxs on hosted streaming since ~2026-03-16T14:05Z. ~120 failed streams in 10m window, errors look like `connection reset by peer` and HTTP 502/503. SDK v0.9.2 (node), region: us-east-1. Customer says it started right after a spike of concurrent users. Can SRE / runtime look? trace ids: trace-0a1b2c3d, trace-0f9e8d7c

Sam: oncall here. Can you paste a representative request (headers + minimal payload) and any client-side retry behavior? Also want the p95 lat and number of streams concurrently hitting the pool at the time.

Elly: Repro snippet from customer (redacted keys):
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --http2 https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":true}'
```
Server log sample: `2026-03-16T14:05:21Z [req=trace-0a1b2c3d] upstream error: TLS handshake failed, connection reset by peer`
Customer notes SDK retried 3x quickly (default backoff) then stopped. Also saw billing spike from retries.

deploy-bot: deploy rwd-runtime@2026-03-16-13:52 succeeded (hash abc123)

Priya: thanks. Two quick asks: 1) did this align with that deploy? deploy-bot shows earlier deploy at 13:52, so probably not a hot deploy cause. 2) this smells like an edge TLS/multiplexing issue; we've seen `connection reset` when max concurrent HTTP/2 streams per connection is exceeded or when keepalive timeouts drop sockets under load. Immediate workaround: ask customer to disable streaming (stream:false) for a short window or increase SDK client timeout and add jittered backoff. We'll also try routing their traffic to a lower-concurrency pool.

Marcus: infra metrics show us-east-1 edge proxy (front-sni-3) had a FD and connection spike 14:03-14:07 — fd_count +27% and http2 RST_STREAM rate up. Heap usage on proxy nodes spiked ~75%->92% for ~4m, GC thrashing visible.

Priya: repro from our side (intermittent): run the same curl with `--http2 --header "Connection: keep-alive"` and a short interval loop x100. Observed ~30% of streams fail within 100 requests with `RST_STREAM` then `connection reset`. If we force single-stream connections (no multiplex) failures drop to <5%.

Elly: Customer update sent: "We're seeing intermittent connection resets on streaming endpoints; engineering is investigating and we've routed your traffic to a lower-concurrency pool as a temporary mitigation. Please switch to non-streaming calls if possible while we fix the root cause. We'll follow up with a timeline." They asked about credits for retries.

Tom: CSM here — I've proposed a one-off credit and a follow-up call tomorrow. Please flag if this becomes a broader incident so I can escalate with customer leadership.

Sam: I opened incident INC-2026-3145, assigned to Priya and Marcus. Next steps: collect full heap/GC traces from front-sni-3 around 14:00-14:10, capture edge TLS log level for the window, and validate whether a traffic shaping rule moved them off the hot nodes. Also need a short-lived mitigation: route customer to dedicated low-concurrency pool (done) + ask SDK team to ship a doc snippet for non-streaming fallback.

Elly: INC-2026-3145 confirmed. I'll post repro logs and customer's SDK stacktrace to the ticket. Will update customer after we confirm root cause and ETA.

Priya: I'll grab heap dumps and enable verbose TLS logging for 30m. Marcus will look at LB config and autoscaler behavior.

Marcus: queued a rolling restart of 2 affected front-sni nodes to clear GC thrash; monitoring for recovery.

Elly: thanks team — keeping customer updated. Will close the loop here once we have RCA or broader impact.
